Intended use: Second-opinion urgency triage for inbound job descriptions; fallback when the LLM is unavailable. Not for life-safety decisions (the deterministic safety net and the LLM handle those).
Data: 1800 synthetic historical jobs; time-based split (1350 train / 450 test). Labels are dispatcher-assigned; agreement with true urgency on test = 0.893 (the practical accuracy ceiling).
Selected: tfidf_logreg_calibrated (promoted v2 to champion (log_loss=0.4133 vs None)). Rule: best macro-F1, ties within one CV std go to the lower log loss, because the agent acts on the confidence.
Limitations: Templated synthetic text inflates accuracy vs real messages.
Retrain/evaluate on paraphrased and production-derived data.
Emergency recall is the metric to watch; tune thresholds for it.
Trained on job descriptions, applied to customer messages: domain shift. Vague messages ('something is broken') get overconfident scores, so the agent may only upgrade urgency, never downgrade.
